title: JSON pages
description: A page tree that exists as data: page.json is the snapshot, page.jsonl is the delta log.

blocks.text:
Everything below the line came out of `page.json` — this paragraph, the three pages in the rail, and the pages inside those. No `page.js` was written for any of them.

The snapshot is one node: `title`, `icon`, `description`, `blocks`, and a `children` object of more nodes of the same shape. `Page.declare()` already takes that shape, so the tree is real pages with real urls the moment it is fetched.

format.title: The format
format.description: One node shape, one delta line shape. That is the whole spec.

blocks.text:
Two files beside each other. The **snapshot** is the state; the **log** is what happened to it since.

```
page.json    the tree, as one node
page.jsonl   one delta per line, append only
```

Loading is `fetch` the snapshot, replay the log in order. Compacting writes the replayed state back as the snapshot and empties the log — which is why the json never grows past the tree it describes.

snapshot.title: Snapshot
snapshot.description: page.json — the tree as one nested node.

blocks.text: A node is a page. Its `children` are pages. There is no separate "page list" and no ids — the object key is the url segment, the way a directory name is.

shape.title: The node
shape.description: Three levels deep, from data alone — this page is the third.

deltas.title: Deltas
deltas.description: page.jsonl — one line per change, appended, never rewritten.

blocks.text:
One line, three ops:

```json
{"at": "2026-08-30T18:00:00-05:00", "op": "set", "path": ["children", "format", "title"], "value": "The format"}
```

- **set** — `path` ends at the field, `value` replaces it.
- **del** — `path` ends at the field or the array index; it goes away.
- **append** — `path` ends at an ARRAY, `value` is pushed onto it. A new paragraph is one line.

An edit costs one line. Nothing rewrites the snapshot, so two edits a second are two appends, not two copies of the tree.

why.title: Why json plus jsonl
why.description: The snapshot keeps the file small; the log keeps every change.

blocks.text:
A json file you rewrite on every edit is a file that loses its history and still grows — every save is a whole-tree write, and the diff is the whole tree.

A jsonl you only ever append to keeps the history and never conflicts, but replaying ten thousand lines to draw a page is not a page load.

Together: the snapshot bounds the read, the log bounds the write. **Compaction** is the one moment they meet — the replayed state becomes the new snapshot and the log starts again at zero bytes.

limits.title: What data cannot do
limits.description: Content blocks, yes. Behaviour needs js — and here is the hatch.

blocks.text:
A block names a **renderer**: `{ "type": "cards" }` draws this page's children as cards, because a function called `cards` is registered in `json.js`. Data chooses; js supplies.

So a page made of data can say anything a registered renderer can draw, and nothing else. A page that needs its own `render()`, its own state, its own event handlers is a `page.js` — and it can still live in this tree as one more child.

The honest line is in the [readme](/imagine/cms/json/readme/).
